title: Cross-validation failure: small sample sizes lead to large error bars
study_context: Methodological study of small-sample cross-validation, motivated by brain imaging.
population_or_data: Methodological study of small-sample cross-validation, motivated by brain imaging.
main_findings: Small-sample cross-validation can have substantial uncertainty, and standard errors calculated across folds can underestimate that uncertainty.
limitations: Selected-page review only: PDF p.1, Abstract. Text extracted and page visually checked on 2026-10-07.
Acquired 2017 arXiv v1 author preprint; bibliographic year 2018 is the published NeuroImage article.
Transfer to cardiac WSI MIL requires qualification.
does_not_establish: Does not provide an SMC-specific AP confidence interval, justify transplanting a reported neuroimaging error bar, or make 575 events independent patients.
relevance_to_project: Fold or seed variability is not a substitute for uncertainty over independent patients.
